hi.meaning: हे पार्थ, श्रद्धा के बिना किया गया हवन, दान, तप और जो कुछ भी किया जाए, वह असत् कहा जाता है। उसका फल न यहाँ होता है, न मरने के बाद।

en.body: O Partha, sacrifice, charity, austerity, and any deed done without trust are called unreal. Its fruit exists neither here nor after death. Krishna calls all of it asat, unreal. A sacrifice, a gift, or a penance done without faith is not just empty; it is called unreal, with no fruit here or after death. Arjuna then asks about the exact truth of renunciation and relinquishment.

issues: meaning_changed: "उसका फल न यहाँ होता है, न मरने के बाद।" (The source explicitly states 'न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह' (neither after death nor here), whereas the Hindi translation drops 'here' (न यहाँ होता है), changing the scope of the verse to only mention the afterlife.)

meaning_changed: "उसका फल न यहाँ होता है, न मरने के बाद।" (The Hindi meaning drops the explicit 'unreal' (असत्) label for the fruit, whereas the English source explicitly states 'Its fruit exists neither here nor after death'. The Hindi meaning merely states the fruit is not here or after death, softening the source's declaration that the fruit itself is unreal (asat).)

wrong_fact: "अर्जुन फिर पूछते हैं कि त्याग और संन्यास के बारे में सही सच क्या है।" (The previous verse (27) was spoken by Krishna, not Arjuna. The notice incorrectly attributes the question about renunciation to Arjuna, misstating the listener/speaker relationship for this section.)
